title: OWASP Top 10 on the front-end: XSS, CSRF and clickjacking

videos.script:
This lesson is about three attacks that belong to the browser. {{three}} And each is shown in the planner, with a witness that proves the flaw and does nothing else.

First, text that becomes code. {{note}} The planner gains a note on each session, written the quick way, with innerHTML. A note with a bold tag in it comes out bold. The page built an element from what a person typed. One word fixes it: textContent.

Second, a request your browser sends for another site. {{csrf}} The planner's cookie already has two defences. You add a third, on the server: a request that changes something must come from the planner's own origin.

Third, a page inside another page. {{frame}} One line of last lesson's policy stops it, and now a test proves it, with a control beside it.

Last, the code you did not write. {{supply}} Over a hundred packages, for one small script.
